semantic_validation.evidence_scope: Current first-party Scopus Support Center documentation plus bounded known-query contrasts in the authorized rendered public UI on the validation date. Counts are observations, not fixtures.

raw_query.representation: One caller-supplied Scopus Advanced Search expression in the native Monaco editor; this adapter never rewrites its grammar.
raw_query.unqualified_scope: The official help equates an unqualified expression with ALL(...); specific field codes narrow the indexed fields and can exclude records with missing fields.

field_codes.case: Field codes may be upper- or lowercase, with exact spelling including hyphens.

boolean.parentheses: Explicit parentheses override the native precedence.

queries: TITLE("tidal energy" OR "marine energy" AND "power plant")
TITLE(("tidal energy" OR "marine energy") AND "power plant")
TITLE("tidal energy" OR ("marine energy" AND "power plant"))
live_contrast.observation: The two OR-grouped queries returned 2 and 809 records, respectively; the unparenthesized query returned 2.

boolean.parser_caveat: The current help warns that complex/ambiguous combinations of Boolean, proximity, wildcards, and filters may be rejected or time out after the 2025 parser changes; a source error remains an error, not zero results.

wildcards.meaning: A wildcard/truncation character that expands matching word forms; the official examples show broader trailing expansion.
wildcards.placement: It must be attached to a word, not used alone.  The current help warns against double truncation and against placing dot/slash/hyphen between a wildcard and a word because the wildcard is dropped.
wildcards.loose_phrase: Wildcards are supported in a loose double-quoted phrase.
wildcards.exact_phrase: Inside braces, wildcard characters are searched literally rather than expanded.

other_symbols.reason: The current first-party pages used for this audit document * but do not establish a second wildcard symbol.

wildcards.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energ*") returned 816 versus 809 for TITLE("tidal energy"); TITLE({tidal energ*}) was an explicit zero state.

question_mark.documented_state: The current help documents * expansion. Its exact-phrase example shows a question mark as a literal character; it does not publish a single-character wildcard contract.

live_documents_contrast.observation: The equal Documents totals do not distinguish punctuation being ignored from a single-character expansion.

question_mark.safe_boundary: Do not treat ? as an expansion operator in a typed control or raw query until current Scopus documentation and a discriminating known-item contrast establish it.

secondary_documents.source_boundary: Official Scopus guidance says Secondary Documents are references to non-indexed items with incomplete or inconsistent metadata. A displayed title is not proof that the same title is fully indexed.
secondary_documents.readback_contract: Each retained state below had exact native Monaco editor readback before Submit, the matching advancedQuery echo, selected dm scope, and a native plf-t readback where a positive state exposed a sort.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_loose_trailing_wildcard

known_item.title: Studies on glucosaminidase. 4. the fluorimetric assay on N-acetyl-β-glucosaminidase

contrasts.finding: A trailing * inside a loose TITLE phrase produced a positive Secondary state and included a visible known secondary title.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The same query was not promoted to a complete Secondary export; the source's partial reference metadata and current rendered scope remain separate.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_exact_wildcard_literal
contrasts.finding: The same * spelling inside exact braces was an explicit Secondary zero, consistent with the official literal-wildcard rule.
contrasts.safe_boundary: This is a bounded known-item contrast, not proof that every exact wildcard expression is a source zero.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_hyphen_before_wildcard
contrasts.finding: The hyphen-before-wildcard form was an explicit Secondary zero in this bounded check.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The zero does not establish whether the wildcard was dropped, whether the remaining term matched, or a field-specific parser rule.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_loose_trailing_wildcard
contrasts.finding: The loose phrase with trailing * reached a positive Secondary state and reported 85, but only five identifiable rows were rendered for the 1--10 range in this snapshot.
contrasts.safe_boundary: Treat the wildcard acceptance and source total as semantic evidence; treat row membership/completeness as unknown and do not export this sparse page as a complete result set.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_exact_wildcard_literal
contrasts.finding: The exact-braced INDEXTERMS wildcard form was an explicit Secondary zero.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The official literal-character rule is supported for this bounded known term, but no general Secondary indexed-term vocabulary is claimed.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_bare_trailing_wildcard_unresolved
contrasts.finding: The bounded Secondary transition did not expose a stable total/range for the bare trailing-wildcard form.
contrasts.safe_boundary: This is unknown, not zero: the state may reflect hydration, indexing lag, rate/challenge behavior, or a source query limitation.

contrasts.name: secondary_question_mark_loose_unresolved
contrasts.finding: The bounded Secondary transition exposed no stable total/range for the question-mark form.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The current official help documents * expansion but does not establish ? as a single-character expansion; do not promote this to either behavior.

secondary_documents.safe_interpretation: The positive loose-phrase contrasts establish bounded acceptance of a trailing * in the current Secondary UI. Exact-braced zeros are consistent with literal wildcard characters. The hyphen-boundary zero does not prove whether Scopus dropped the wildcard or whether the remaining term matched. Bare wildcard and ? transitions with no stable total/range are unknown, not zero.

automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.finding: The current help says Scopus uses lemmatization for English words and most scientific terms except exact phrases, and that loose phrases include plurals/spelling variants.
automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energies") and TITLE("tidal energy") each returned 809; this is a bounded English title observation.
automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.exactness_caveat: No global synonym or all-language guarantee is claimed; analyzer, field, language, and exact-phrase mode can change expansion.

hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.finding: Outside exact braces, the current help treats a hyphen as punctuation and says loose phrase punctuation is ignored/normalized; exact braces retain included punctuation.
hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal-energy") and TITLE("tidal/energy") each returned 809, while TITLE({tidal-energy}) returned 4 versus 781 for TITLE({tidal energy}).
hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.boundary: Do not generalize equivalence to every field or punctuation sequence; the raw spelling is preserved.

loose.syntax: Straight double quotes, for example "heart attack".
loose.meaning: A loose/approximate phrase keeps terms together while allowing documented variants and wildcard use.

exact.meaning: Stop words, spaces, and punctuation inside braces are included; wildcards are literal.

phrases.quotation_marks: Use straight ASCII double quotes; curly quotes can produce a parsing error.
phrases.live_contrast: TITLE({tidal energy}) returned 781 versus 809 for the loose TITLE("tidal energy") query.

syntax.W/n: Terms within the specified distance in either order.
syntax.PRE/n: Terms within the specified distance with the first preceding the second.

proximity.precedence: Between OR and AND in the documented precedence order.

counting.finding: For the indexed title Tidal dissipation of energy, W/1 did not include the title, while W/2 and W/3 did; the two intervening tokens make this a bounded observation that n counts the maximum intervening indexed words for this case.
counting.unknown: The source does not define a universal tokenizer for stop words, punctuation, or every language/field; do not apply the observation as a client-side token counter.

proximity.direction: PRE is directional: the forward PRE/2 query included the known title and the reversed PRE/2 query did not include it in the bounded oldest-first known-item check.
proximity.source_caveat: The current help warns against putting an exact phrase on one side of a proximity operator.

article_document_types.meaning: Restricts Scopus document types using source codes.
article_document_types.result_refinement: The rendered Documents result page separately exposes a native Document type facet; its visible label/state is not substituted for raw DOCTYPE syntax.
article_document_types.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") AND DOCTYPE(ar) returned 482 of the 809-record bounded title baseline.

language.meaning: The language in which the original document was written.
language.result_refinement: Language is also a native rendered result facet when the requested label is visibly available; facet selection is a result refinement, not an invented query clause.
language.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") AND LANGUAGE(english) returned 755 versus the 809-record bounded title baseline.
language.unknown: No complete language-code normalization or cross-language expansion rule is claimed.

PUBYEAR.meaning: Numeric publication year; the current help notes that it includes in-press records assigned to a publication year even without a finalized publication date.
PUBYEAR.boundary: AFT/BEF are strict source comparisons; IS selects the named year.
PUBYEAR.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") returned 809; adding PUBYEAR AFT 1971 returned 802, while PUBYEAR IS 1972 returned 3.

PUBDATETXT.precision: Publisher-supplied free-text date, commonly month/year but not standardized.
PUBDATETXT.meaning: Matches the date string supplied by the publisher; the official example is PUBDATETXT(July 2004).
PUBDATETXT.boundary: No calendar inclusivity or timezone is inferred from this text field.

LOAD-DATE.precision: Calendar day, represented in the documented YYYYMMDD examples.
LOAD-DATE.meaning: The day the record was added to Scopus or reprocessed.

adapter_year_bounds.implementation: --year-start/--year-end are source-side and inclusive by emitting PUBYEAR > (start - 1) and PUBYEAR < (end + 1).
adapter_year_bounds.live_contrast: The raw rendered query with PUBYEAR > 1971 and PUBYEAR < 1973 returned the same 3-record 1972 state as PUBYEAR IS 1972.

timezone.reason: The current first-party documentation and rendered date fields expose calendar values but no publication/load-date timezone or time-of-day contract; this adapter performs no timezone conversion.

unknowns: Analyzer-specific morphology, synonym expansion, and punctuation behavior outside the bounded English title contrasts.
A universal proximity tokenizer across fields, languages, stop words, and punctuation.
Whether the observed hyphen/dot/slash wildcard warning is equivalent in every field and result scope; the Secondary hyphen-boundary zero is not an equivalence proof.
Secondary Documents wildcard behavior for bare trailing * and the unproved ? form when the current UI exposes no stable total/range.
Whether a displayed Secondary title is searchable in the same way as its partial reference metadata; sparse rendered rows are not a complete stable-ID ledger.
A Scopus date timezone or time-of-day interpretation.

semantic_validation.evidence_scope: Current first-party Scopus Support Center documentation plus bounded known-query contrasts in the authorized rendered public UI on the validation date. Counts are observations, not fixtures.

raw_query.representation: One caller-supplied Scopus Advanced Search expression in the native Monaco editor; this adapter never rewrites its grammar.
raw_query.unqualified_scope: The official help equates an unqualified expression with ALL(...); specific field codes narrow the indexed fields and can exclude records with missing fields.

field_codes.case: Field codes may be upper- or lowercase, with exact spelling including hyphens.

boolean.parentheses: Explicit parentheses override the native precedence.

queries: TITLE("tidal energy" OR "marine energy" AND "power plant")
TITLE(("tidal energy" OR "marine energy") AND "power plant")
TITLE("tidal energy" OR ("marine energy" AND "power plant"))
live_contrast.observation: The two OR-grouped queries returned 2 and 809 records, respectively; the unparenthesized query returned 2.

boolean.parser_caveat: The current help warns that complex/ambiguous combinations of Boolean, proximity, wildcards, and filters may be rejected or time out after the 2025 parser changes; a source error remains an error, not zero results.

wildcards.meaning: A wildcard/truncation character that expands matching word forms; the official examples show broader trailing expansion.
wildcards.placement: It must be attached to a word, not used alone.  The current help warns against double truncation and against placing dot/slash/hyphen between a wildcard and a word because the wildcard is dropped.
wildcards.loose_phrase: Wildcards are supported in a loose double-quoted phrase.
wildcards.exact_phrase: Inside braces, wildcard characters are searched literally rather than expanded.

other_symbols.reason: The current first-party pages used for this audit document * but do not establish a second wildcard symbol.

wildcards.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energ*") returned 816 versus 809 for TITLE("tidal energy"); TITLE({tidal energ*}) was an explicit zero state.

question_mark.documented_state: The current help documents * expansion. Its exact-phrase example shows a question mark as a literal character; it does not publish a single-character wildcard contract.

live_documents_contrast.observation: The equal Documents totals do not distinguish punctuation being ignored from a single-character expansion.

question_mark.safe_boundary: Do not treat ? as an expansion operator in a typed control or raw query until current Scopus documentation and a discriminating known-item contrast establish it.

secondary_documents.source_boundary: Official Scopus guidance says Secondary Documents are references to non-indexed items with incomplete or inconsistent metadata. A displayed title is not proof that the same title is fully indexed.
secondary_documents.readback_contract: Each retained state below had exact native Monaco editor readback before Submit, the matching advancedQuery echo, selected dm scope, and a native plf-t readback where a positive state exposed a sort.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_loose_trailing_wildcard

known_item.title: Studies on glucosaminidase. 4. the fluorimetric assay on N-acetyl-β-glucosaminidase

contrasts.finding: A trailing * inside a loose TITLE phrase produced a positive Secondary state and included a visible known secondary title.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The same query was not promoted to a complete Secondary export; the source's partial reference metadata and current rendered scope remain separate.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_exact_wildcard_literal
contrasts.finding: The same * spelling inside exact braces was an explicit Secondary zero, consistent with the official literal-wildcard rule.
contrasts.safe_boundary: This is a bounded known-item contrast, not proof that every exact wildcard expression is a source zero.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_hyphen_before_wildcard
contrasts.finding: The hyphen-before-wildcard form was an explicit Secondary zero in this bounded check.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The zero does not establish whether the wildcard was dropped, whether the remaining term matched, or a field-specific parser rule.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_loose_trailing_wildcard
contrasts.finding: The loose phrase with trailing * reached a positive Secondary state and reported 85, but only five identifiable rows were rendered for the 1--10 range in this snapshot.
contrasts.safe_boundary: Treat the wildcard acceptance and source total as semantic evidence; treat row membership/completeness as unknown and do not export this sparse page as a complete result set.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_exact_wildcard_literal
contrasts.finding: The exact-braced INDEXTERMS wildcard form was an explicit Secondary zero.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The official literal-character rule is supported for this bounded known term, but no general Secondary indexed-term vocabulary is claimed.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_bare_trailing_wildcard_unresolved
contrasts.finding: The bounded Secondary transition did not expose a stable total/range for the bare trailing-wildcard form.
contrasts.safe_boundary: This is unknown, not zero: the state may reflect hydration, indexing lag, rate/challenge behavior, or a source query limitation.

contrasts.name: secondary_question_mark_loose_unresolved
contrasts.finding: The bounded Secondary transition exposed no stable total/range for the question-mark form.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The current official help documents * expansion but does not establish ? as a single-character expansion; do not promote this to either behavior.

secondary_documents.safe_interpretation: The positive loose-phrase contrasts establish bounded acceptance of a trailing * in the current Secondary UI. Exact-braced zeros are consistent with literal wildcard characters. The hyphen-boundary zero does not prove whether Scopus dropped the wildcard or whether the remaining term matched. Bare wildcard and ? transitions with no stable total/range are unknown, not zero.

automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.finding: The current help says Scopus uses lemmatization for English words and most scientific terms except exact phrases, and that loose phrases include plurals/spelling variants.
automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energies") and TITLE("tidal energy") each returned 809; this is a bounded English title observation.
automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.exactness_caveat: No global synonym or all-language guarantee is claimed; analyzer, field, language, and exact-phrase mode can change expansion.

hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.finding: Outside exact braces, the current help treats a hyphen as punctuation and says loose phrase punctuation is ignored/normalized; exact braces retain included punctuation.
hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal-energy") and TITLE("tidal/energy") each returned 809, while TITLE({tidal-energy}) returned 4 versus 781 for TITLE({tidal energy}).
hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.boundary: Do not generalize equivalence to every field or punctuation sequence; the raw spelling is preserved.

loose.syntax: Straight double quotes, for example "heart attack".
loose.meaning: A loose/approximate phrase keeps terms together while allowing documented variants and wildcard use.

exact.meaning: Stop words, spaces, and punctuation inside braces are included; wildcards are literal.

phrases.quotation_marks: Use straight ASCII double quotes; curly quotes can produce a parsing error.
phrases.live_contrast: TITLE({tidal energy}) returned 781 versus 809 for the loose TITLE("tidal energy") query.

syntax.W/n: Terms within the specified distance in either order.
syntax.PRE/n: Terms within the specified distance with the first preceding the second.

proximity.precedence: Between OR and AND in the documented precedence order.

counting.finding: For the indexed title Tidal dissipation of energy, W/1 did not include the title, while W/2 and W/3 did; the two intervening tokens make this a bounded observation that n counts the maximum intervening indexed words for this case.
counting.unknown: The source does not define a universal tokenizer for stop words, punctuation, or every language/field; do not apply the observation as a client-side token counter.

proximity.direction: PRE is directional: the forward PRE/2 query included the known title and the reversed PRE/2 query did not include it in the bounded oldest-first known-item check.
proximity.source_caveat: The current help warns against putting an exact phrase on one side of a proximity operator.

article_document_types.meaning: Restricts Scopus document types using source codes.
article_document_types.result_refinement: The rendered Documents result page separately exposes a native Document type facet; its visible label/state is not substituted for raw DOCTYPE syntax.
article_document_types.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") AND DOCTYPE(ar) returned 482 of the 809-record bounded title baseline.

language.meaning: The language in which the original document was written.
language.result_refinement: Language is also a native rendered result facet when the requested label is visibly available; facet selection is a result refinement, not an invented query clause.
language.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") AND LANGUAGE(english) returned 755 versus the 809-record bounded title baseline.
language.unknown: No complete language-code normalization or cross-language expansion rule is claimed.

PUBYEAR.meaning: Numeric publication year; the current help notes that it includes in-press records assigned to a publication year even without a finalized publication date.
PUBYEAR.boundary: AFT/BEF are strict source comparisons; IS selects the named year.
PUBYEAR.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") returned 809; adding PUBYEAR AFT 1971 returned 802, while PUBYEAR IS 1972 returned 3.

PUBDATETXT.precision: Publisher-supplied free-text date, commonly month/year but not standardized.
PUBDATETXT.meaning: Matches the date string supplied by the publisher; the official example is PUBDATETXT(July 2004).
PUBDATETXT.boundary: No calendar inclusivity or timezone is inferred from this text field.

LOAD-DATE.precision: Calendar day, represented in the documented YYYYMMDD examples.
LOAD-DATE.meaning: The day the record was added to Scopus or reprocessed.

adapter_year_bounds.implementation: --year-start/--year-end are source-side and inclusive by emitting PUBYEAR > (start - 1) and PUBYEAR < (end + 1).
adapter_year_bounds.live_contrast: The raw rendered query with PUBYEAR > 1971 and PUBYEAR < 1973 returned the same 3-record 1972 state as PUBYEAR IS 1972.

timezone.reason: The current first-party documentation and rendered date fields expose calendar values but no publication/load-date timezone or time-of-day contract; this adapter performs no timezone conversion.

unknowns: Analyzer-specific morphology, synonym expansion, and punctuation behavior outside the bounded English title contrasts.
A universal proximity tokenizer across fields, languages, stop words, and punctuation.
Whether the observed hyphen/dot/slash wildcard warning is equivalent in every field and result scope; the Secondary hyphen-boundary zero is not an equivalence proof.
Secondary Documents wildcard behavior for bare trailing * and the unproved ? form when the current UI exposes no stable total/range.
Whether a displayed Secondary title is searchable in the same way as its partial reference metadata; sparse rendered rows are not a complete stable-ID ledger.
A Scopus date timezone or time-of-day interpretation.

semantic_validation.evidence_scope: Current first-party Scopus Support Center documentation plus bounded known-query contrasts in the authorized rendered public UI on the validation date. Counts are observations, not fixtures.

raw_query.representation: One caller-supplied Scopus Advanced Search expression in the native Monaco editor; this adapter never rewrites its grammar.
raw_query.unqualified_scope: The official help equates an unqualified expression with ALL(...); specific field codes narrow the indexed fields and can exclude records with missing fields.

field_codes.case: Field codes may be upper- or lowercase, with exact spelling including hyphens.

boolean.parentheses: Explicit parentheses override the native precedence.

queries: TITLE("tidal energy" OR "marine energy" AND "power plant")
TITLE(("tidal energy" OR "marine energy") AND "power plant")
TITLE("tidal energy" OR ("marine energy" AND "power plant"))
live_contrast.observation: The two OR-grouped queries returned 2 and 809 records, respectively; the unparenthesized query returned 2.

boolean.parser_caveat: The current help warns that complex/ambiguous combinations of Boolean, proximity, wildcards, and filters may be rejected or time out after the 2025 parser changes; a source error remains an error, not zero results.

wildcards.meaning: A wildcard/truncation character that expands matching word forms; the official examples show broader trailing expansion.
wildcards.placement: It must be attached to a word, not used alone.  The current help warns against double truncation and against placing dot/slash/hyphen between a wildcard and a word because the wildcard is dropped.
wildcards.loose_phrase: Wildcards are supported in a loose double-quoted phrase.
wildcards.exact_phrase: Inside braces, wildcard characters are searched literally rather than expanded.

other_symbols.reason: The current first-party pages used for this audit document * but do not establish a second wildcard symbol.

wildcards.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energ*") returned 816 versus 809 for TITLE("tidal energy"); TITLE({tidal energ*}) was an explicit zero state.

question_mark.documented_state: The current help documents * expansion. Its exact-phrase example shows a question mark as a literal character; it does not publish a single-character wildcard contract.

live_documents_contrast.observation: The equal Documents totals do not distinguish punctuation being ignored from a single-character expansion.

question_mark.safe_boundary: Do not treat ? as an expansion operator in a typed control or raw query until current Scopus documentation and a discriminating known-item contrast establish it.

secondary_documents.source_boundary: Official Scopus guidance says Secondary Documents are references to non-indexed items with incomplete or inconsistent metadata. A displayed title is not proof that the same title is fully indexed.
secondary_documents.readback_contract: Each retained state below had exact native Monaco editor readback before Submit, the matching advancedQuery echo, selected dm scope, and a native plf-t readback where a positive state exposed a sort.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_loose_trailing_wildcard

known_item.title: Studies on glucosaminidase. 4. the fluorimetric assay on N-acetyl-β-glucosaminidase

contrasts.finding: A trailing * inside a loose TITLE phrase produced a positive Secondary state and included a visible known secondary title.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The same query was not promoted to a complete Secondary export; the source's partial reference metadata and current rendered scope remain separate.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_exact_wildcard_literal
contrasts.finding: The same * spelling inside exact braces was an explicit Secondary zero, consistent with the official literal-wildcard rule.
contrasts.safe_boundary: This is a bounded known-item contrast, not proof that every exact wildcard expression is a source zero.

contrasts.name: secondary_title_hyphen_before_wildcard
contrasts.finding: The hyphen-before-wildcard form was an explicit Secondary zero in this bounded check.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The zero does not establish whether the wildcard was dropped, whether the remaining term matched, or a field-specific parser rule.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_loose_trailing_wildcard
contrasts.finding: The loose phrase with trailing * reached a positive Secondary state and reported 85, but only five identifiable rows were rendered for the 1--10 range in this snapshot.
contrasts.safe_boundary: Treat the wildcard acceptance and source total as semantic evidence; treat row membership/completeness as unknown and do not export this sparse page as a complete result set.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_exact_wildcard_literal
contrasts.finding: The exact-braced INDEXTERMS wildcard form was an explicit Secondary zero.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The official literal-character rule is supported for this bounded known term, but no general Secondary indexed-term vocabulary is claimed.

contrasts.name: secondary_index_terms_bare_trailing_wildcard_unresolved
contrasts.finding: The bounded Secondary transition did not expose a stable total/range for the bare trailing-wildcard form.
contrasts.safe_boundary: This is unknown, not zero: the state may reflect hydration, indexing lag, rate/challenge behavior, or a source query limitation.

contrasts.name: secondary_question_mark_loose_unresolved
contrasts.finding: The bounded Secondary transition exposed no stable total/range for the question-mark form.
contrasts.safe_boundary: The current official help documents * expansion but does not establish ? as a single-character expansion; do not promote this to either behavior.

secondary_documents.safe_interpretation: The positive loose-phrase contrasts establish bounded acceptance of a trailing * in the current Secondary UI. Exact-braced zeros are consistent with literal wildcard characters. The hyphen-boundary zero does not prove whether Scopus dropped the wildcard or whether the remaining term matched. Bare wildcard and ? transitions with no stable total/range are unknown, not zero.

automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.finding: The current help says Scopus uses lemmatization for English words and most scientific terms except exact phrases, and that loose phrases include plurals/spelling variants.
automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energies") and TITLE("tidal energy") each returned 809; this is a bounded English title observation.
automatic_plurals_stemming_variants.exactness_caveat: No global synonym or all-language guarantee is claimed; analyzer, field, language, and exact-phrase mode can change expansion.

hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.finding: Outside exact braces, the current help treats a hyphen as punctuation and says loose phrase punctuation is ignored/normalized; exact braces retain included punctuation.
hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal-energy") and TITLE("tidal/energy") each returned 809, while TITLE({tidal-energy}) returned 4 versus 781 for TITLE({tidal energy}).
hyphens_spaces_and_punctuation.boundary: Do not generalize equivalence to every field or punctuation sequence; the raw spelling is preserved.

loose.syntax: Straight double quotes, for example "heart attack".
loose.meaning: A loose/approximate phrase keeps terms together while allowing documented variants and wildcard use.

exact.meaning: Stop words, spaces, and punctuation inside braces are included; wildcards are literal.

phrases.quotation_marks: Use straight ASCII double quotes; curly quotes can produce a parsing error.
phrases.live_contrast: TITLE({tidal energy}) returned 781 versus 809 for the loose TITLE("tidal energy") query.

syntax.W/n: Terms within the specified distance in either order.
syntax.PRE/n: Terms within the specified distance with the first preceding the second.

proximity.precedence: Between OR and AND in the documented precedence order.

counting.finding: For the indexed title Tidal dissipation of energy, W/1 did not include the title, while W/2 and W/3 did; the two intervening tokens make this a bounded observation that n counts the maximum intervening indexed words for this case.
counting.unknown: The source does not define a universal tokenizer for stop words, punctuation, or every language/field; do not apply the observation as a client-side token counter.

proximity.direction: PRE is directional: the forward PRE/2 query included the known title and the reversed PRE/2 query did not include it in the bounded oldest-first known-item check.
proximity.source_caveat: The current help warns against putting an exact phrase on one side of a proximity operator.

article_document_types.meaning: Restricts Scopus document types using source codes.
article_document_types.result_refinement: The rendered Documents result page separately exposes a native Document type facet; its visible label/state is not substituted for raw DOCTYPE syntax.
article_document_types.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") AND DOCTYPE(ar) returned 482 of the 809-record bounded title baseline.

language.meaning: The language in which the original document was written.
language.result_refinement: Language is also a native rendered result facet when the requested label is visibly available; facet selection is a result refinement, not an invented query clause.
language.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") AND LANGUAGE(english) returned 755 versus the 809-record bounded title baseline.
language.unknown: No complete language-code normalization or cross-language expansion rule is claimed.

PUBYEAR.meaning: Numeric publication year; the current help notes that it includes in-press records assigned to a publication year even without a finalized publication date.
PUBYEAR.boundary: AFT/BEF are strict source comparisons; IS selects the named year.
PUBYEAR.live_contrast: TITLE("tidal energy") returned 809; adding PUBYEAR AFT 1971 returned 802, while PUBYEAR IS 1972 returned 3.

PUBDATETXT.precision: Publisher-supplied free-text date, commonly month/year but not standardized.
PUBDATETXT.meaning: Matches the date string supplied by the publisher; the official example is PUBDATETXT(July 2004).
PUBDATETXT.boundary: No calendar inclusivity or timezone is inferred from this text field.

LOAD-DATE.precision: Calendar day, represented in the documented YYYYMMDD examples.
LOAD-DATE.meaning: The day the record was added to Scopus or reprocessed.

adapter_year_bounds.implementation: --year-start/--year-end are source-side and inclusive by emitting PUBYEAR > (start - 1) and PUBYEAR < (end + 1).
adapter_year_bounds.live_contrast: The raw rendered query with PUBYEAR > 1971 and PUBYEAR < 1973 returned the same 3-record 1972 state as PUBYEAR IS 1972.

timezone.reason: The current first-party documentation and rendered date fields expose calendar values but no publication/load-date timezone or time-of-day contract; this adapter performs no timezone conversion.

unknowns: Analyzer-specific morphology, synonym expansion, and punctuation behavior outside the bounded English title contrasts.
A universal proximity tokenizer across fields, languages, stop words, and punctuation.
Whether the observed hyphen/dot/slash wildcard warning is equivalent in every field and result scope; the Secondary hyphen-boundary zero is not an equivalence proof.
Secondary Documents wildcard behavior for bare trailing * and the unproved ? form when the current UI exposes no stable total/range.
Whether a displayed Secondary title is searchable in the same way as its partial reference metadata; sparse rendered rows are not a complete stable-ID ledger.
A Scopus date timezone or time-of-day interpretation.
